title: Quasi-affine scheme descent over the open image of an affine etale map
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $a:T'\to T$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] between affine $S$-schemes, let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] with a morphism $X\to T$, and let $W\subseteq X$ be an open subspace, meaning that its inclusion becomes an open immersion on every scheme base change [def-weil-open-immersion]. For an algebraic space $Y$, $|Y|$ is its set of field-valued point classes, two maps from field spectra being identified when they agree over a common field extension. Let $B\subseteq T$ be the open subscheme with $|B|=\operatorname{im}(|T'|\to|T|)$, and suppose the image of $|W|\to|T|$ is contained in $|B|$. Suppose $P=W\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is represented by a scheme whose structure map $P\to T'$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism], meaning that the inverse image of each affine open is a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Then $W\to T$ factors through $B$, and the induced map $p:T'\to B$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], surjective etale and both a singleton fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] and an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site]. The functor on schemes over $B$ sending $Q\to B$ to the $S$-morphisms $Q\to W$ over $B$ is an fppf sheaf, and its pullback along $p$ is represented by $P=W\times_BT'$. The canonical comparison $P\times_BT'\simeq T'\times_BP$, identifying both with $T'\times_BW\times_BT'$ and retaining the same $W$-section and ordered base coordinates, is a scheme descent datum [def-pd-descent-datum]: on the triple overlap it satisfies $\phi_{02}=\phi_{12}\circ\phi_{01}$. This datum is effective, and there is a $B$-scheme representing the specified sheaf $W$. No affineness assumption on the open scheme $B$ is made.

source.place: Tag 03XW (lemma-neighbourhood-scheme), proof, final paragraph: open image base, covering checks, sheaf descent datum, cocycle and effective descent

proof.text: By [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $W$ is an algebraic space. The image of $a$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], so it defines the stated open subscheme $B\subseteq T$. Regard schemes as their algebraic spaces using [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests] to $W\to T$ and to $a:T\prime\to T$ with open subspace $B$: the assumed point-image containment gives the unique factorization $W\to B$, and the point-image equality gives a factorization $p:T\prime\to B$ which is representable surjective etale. The scheme-test comparison in that lemma identifies $W\times_BT\prime$ with $W\times_TT\prime=P$.

source.place: Tag 03XW, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme, final proof paragraph; expanded using Tags 03IE, 01S8, 01SD, 022C, 02W5 and 0247

proof.text: The one-member affine open cover $\{T\}$ of $T$ has inverse image $T\prime$, which is affine. Thus [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] gives that $a$ is affine. Since $a$ factors through $B$, its pullback along $B\hookrightarrow T$ is $p:T\prime\to B$: the inverse comparison to $T\prime\times_TB\to T\prime$ sends $t$ to $(t,p(t))$, by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Base-change stability of affine morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1) makes $p$ affine (and clause (3) also makes it quasi-compact). This argument uses no affineness of $B$.

source.place: Tag 03XW, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme, final proof paragraph; expanded using Tags 03IE, 01S8, 01SD, 022C, 02W5 and 0247

proof.text: By [def-weil-etale-morphism], the etale morphism $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Together with its surjectivity from Step 1, these are exactly the covering conditions of [def-pc-fppf-site], so $\{p\}$ is an fppf covering. Applying [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] to this singleton family proves that it is also an fpqc covering in the stated sense.

source.place: Tag 03XW, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme, final proof paragraph; expanded using Tags 03IE, 01S8, 01SD, 022C, 02W5 and 0247

proof.text: By [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $W$ is an algebraic space; by [def-trf-algebraic-space] its functor on $S$-schemes is an fppf sheaf. Let $F$ on $B$-schemes be the functor of maps to $W$ over $B$. Given compatible such maps on an fppf covering of a $B$-scheme $Q$, first glue their underlying $S$-maps uniquely in $W$. Their composites to $B$ equal the fixed structure map of $Q$ locally, hence globally because $h_B$ is the representable fppf sheaf of [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. The glued map is therefore over $B$. This proves the sheaf condition for exactly the functor $F$ in the statement, without replacing it by a different sheaf.

source.place: Tag 03XW, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme, final proof paragraph; expanded using Tags 03IE, 01S8, 01SD, 022C, 02W5 and 0247

proof.text: The representation $P=W\times_BT\prime$ of the pullback of $F$ follows on tests: over a map $t:Q\to T\prime$, a map into $P$ is exactly a map $w:Q\to W$ with the same composite to $B$. Apply [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-representability-descent-data] to $F$ and the fppf covering $\{p\}$. Its comparison maps give scheme descent data on the representing scheme $P$. Explicitly, the comparison sends $((w,t_0),t_1)$ to $(t_0,(w,t_1))$; its inverse retains the same $w,t_0,t_1$ and regroups them in the other order. Thus it is the comparison specified in the statement, with the same ordered base coordinates. On a triple overlap, both $\phi_{02}$ and $\phi_{12}\circ\phi_{01}$ retain $w,t_0,t_1,t_2$ and change only the distinguished coordinate from $t_0$ to $t_2$. These natural maps coincide on every test scheme, so the cocycle has the required direction.

source.place: Tag 03XW, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme, final proof paragraph; expanded using Tags 03IE, 01S8, 01SD, 022C, 02W5 and 0247

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-quasi-affine-fpqc-effective-descent] with its $(A,B,V,\phi)$ equal to $(T\prime,B,P,\phi)$. Step 3 supplies its singleton fpqc covering, the hypothesis of this item supplies precisely the quasi-affine morphism $P\to T\prime$, and Step 5 supplies the scheme descent datum and cocycle. It gives a $B$-scheme $V_0$ and an isomorphism $V_0\times_BT\prime\simeq P$ inducing this datum. The cited theorem permits arbitrary scheme base $B$.

source.place: Tag 03XW, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme, final proof paragraph; expanded using Tags 03IE, 01S8, 01SD, 022C, 02W5 and 0247

proof.text: The datum in Step 5 is the datum associated to the specified fppf sheaf $F$. It is effective by Step 6. The final representability criterion of [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-representability-descent-data] therefore says that $F$ itself is represented by a $B$-scheme. This identifies the descended object with the original functor $Q\mapsto\operatorname{Mor}_B(Q,W)$, and proves the last assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q03-4325add30 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the final paragraph of Stacks 03XW (spaces-morphisms.tex, lemma-neighbourhood-scheme) and 02W5 (descent-data-sheaves). The statement is unchanged and faithful to that paragraph: the separatedness and quasi-finiteness that 03XW uses earlier only produce quasi-affineness, which this item assumes. The item is still unsplit in live and side-live, and this is its first delivery. There are no new nodes. The 7 steps checked against the cited statements: (1) 03WT gives the open image B. lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests with J=h_B gives the factorization W→B, gives p representable étale and surjective on every base change, and gives the comparison W×_B T'≅W×_T T'=P. (2) 01S8 on the cover {T} makes a affine. Since B→T is a monomorphism, p is the base change of a, so permanence clause (1) makes p affine, and no affineness of B is used. (3) Étale plus surjective gives an fppf covering, and 022C makes it fpqc. (4) The sheaf property of F=Mor_B(-,W) is genuinely elementary. (5) h_{T'}×F=h_P. 02W5 gives φ in the direction P×_B T'→T'×_B P, matching def-pd-descent-datum, and the explicit cocycle check is correct. (6) 0247 applies with A=T', V=P: the singleton cover is fpqc, P→T' is quasi-affine by hypothesis, and step 5 gives the cocycle. (7) The 02W5 iff gives that F itself is representable. Edge cases T'=∅, a non-surjective, B non-affine and W non-quasi-compact all work. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, there is no cycle and no SGA is cited. I accept the declared tool_uses (the 02W5 and 0247 trf nodes): 03XW itself invokes exactly these lemmas and no node of the unit gives them. Batch-5 flag: I computed the closure of each listed citation. def-a1-space-open-subspace and def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space are general definitions. lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests is a generic algebraic-space open-subspace lemma whose trf closure is only atlas and fibre-product foundations. lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc is a Mathlib leaf (022C). The 02W5 and 0247 nodes are generic descent lemmas. None of their closures reaches a trace-formula or Poincaré theorem, sk-thm-trace-transport or a batch-4 target, and none is given by either assumption, so all are accepted. Minor point, not changed: the statement writes the open-subspace meaning inline and cites def-weil-open-immersion rather than def-a1-space-open-subspace.

lean.statement: theorem openImageQuasiAffineSchemeDescent {S : Scheme.{u}} (T T' : Over S) [IsAffine T.left] [IsAffine T'.left] (a : T' ⟶ T) [Etale a.left] (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (W : OpenSubspace X) (B : Over S) (j : B ⟶ T) [IsOpenImmersion j.left] (hB : pointImage (yoneda.map j) = pointImage (yoneda.map a)) (hW : pointImage (W.val.ι ≫ f) ⊆ pointImage (yoneda.map j)) (P : Over S) (v : P ⟶ T') (q : yoneda.obj P ⟶ W.val.toFunctor) (hP : IsPullback q (yoneda.map v) (W.val.ι ≫ f) (yoneda.map a)) [IsQuasiAffineHom v.left] : ∃ (b : W.val.toFunctor ⟶ yoneda.obj B) (p : T' ⟶ B), b ≫ yoneda.map j = W.val.ι ≫ f ∧ p ≫ j = a ∧ IsAffineHom p.left ∧ Surjective p.left ∧ Etale p.left ∧ Presieve.singleton p.left ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage B.left ∧ Presieve.singleton p.left ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage B.left ∧ IsPullback q (yoneda.map v) b (yoneda.map p) ∧ Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over B.left) (openImageSectionPresheaf B b) ∧ Nonempty (((Over.map p.left).op ⋙ openImageSectionPresheaf B b).RepresentableBy (Over.mk v.left)) ∧ (∃ D : Over.DescentDatum p.left (Over.mk v.left), (∀ (Q : Over S) (m0 m1 : Q ⟶ P) (h : (m0 ≫ v) ≫ p = (m1 ≫ v) ≫ p), (D.transport (m0.left ≫ v.left) (m1.left ≫ v.left) (congrArg (fun k ↦ k.left) h) (Over.homMk m0.left rfl)).left = m1.left ↔ q.app (op Q) m0 = q.app (op Q) m1) ∧ D.IsEffective) ∧ (openImageSectionPresheaf B b).IsRepresentable
lean.note: The helper is the existing restrictedYonedaObj composed with the canonical iterated-slice scheme-test functor. The theorem retains the actual W, both covering claims, the pullback representation, coordinate-preserving canonical descent datum, its effectivity and representability of the specified sheaf over an arbitrary open base B.
